purpose: Website logic, features, operating procedures, and deployment recovery; no personal data
recovery_instruction: Read this file, private Goldenrule project rules, and actual current source before editing. Do not treat pending features as implemented.
storage_policy: Do not store personal data, credentials, tokens, student records, scanned copyrighted pages, or actual financial records in rule files.

sections.heading: QUIZ ROOM — ACTIVE PROJECT COMMAND
sections.rules:
Updated: 2026-11-03
Repository: https://github.com/dezinerj82/Quiz-room
Live site: https://dezinerj82.github.io/Quiz-room/

sections.heading: RESUME IN A NEW CHAT
sections.rules: Continue my Quiz Room project directly in GitHub repository dezinerj82/Quiz-room. Read the latest root goldenrule.txt and inspect the current main branch and relevant files before making changes. This file contains only active exam/quiz rules and how to work with me; the GitHub source files themselves are the authoritative backup for visual design. Preserve all existing functionality and content. Follow my newest instructions, update this file when operational or exam rules change, and never rebuild the project unnecessarily.

sections.heading: HOW TO WORK WITH ME
sections.rules:
- Website navigation hierarchy: Subject -> School Level -> Category (Exercise, Quiz, Exam) -> available quiz sets. Automatically show a school level or category only when it has at least one real playable quiz; hide empty levels/categories, and reveal them when their first quiz is implemented. Keep subjects separate.
- This chat is for making actual GitHub website changes, not generating design images. Screenshots are references for GitHub edits; do not generate images unless explicitly requested.
- Work directly on the repository. Inspect existing code and dependencies before editing, make the smallest safe changes, and preserve all approved functionality and exam questions.
- Production app: root index.html, with active embedded CSS, JavaScript and quiz data. Keep root preview.html synchronized with index.html. Other subject pages redirect to the app. css/ and js/ are retained auxiliary files; images/ holds required assets; backup/ holds legacy/offline files.
- Visual design and appearance are stored in the actual GitHub HTML/CSS/assets, NOT described or duplicated in this command file. Do not re-create visual design from memory or from this text.
- Fetch the latest main branch and file SHAs; make and commit changes safely. Verify saved contents, JavaScript syntax and affected behavior as far as tools allow. Check for regressions, especially quiz launch, answer submission, Next/Resume, bookmarks, timer, scoring and mobile responsiveness.
- A successful commit is NOT proof that GitHub Pages has deployed or that the website was browser-tested. Do not say the live site is Ready without confirming deployment.
- On successful completion and verification of the requested GitHub task, respond ONLY with the green badge: Completed. If the task fails and requires user action, respond with a red badge: Failed - action required, plus brief safe repair options. Always pursue the safest available fix; never leave an error without a clear recovery plan.
- Keep goldenrule.txt current and consolidated. Remove superseded instructions rather than accumulating contradictory historical rules. Do not add purely visual CSS/layout/color/font descriptions here.
- Treat this room as the working conversation for Quiz Room. For quiz-related GitHub implementation requests, make the actual repository changes rather than merely suggesting edits. For questions and planning discussions, answer naturally and concisely; use the completion badge only after a requested implementation has actually been committed and verified as far as available tools allow.
- Communicate in short, clear, direct English. The user prefers minimal commentary and visually simple guidance; avoid long explanations unless requested. Do not address the user by name. Preserve established decisions unless the user explicitly revises them.
- Treat screenshots as references for website modifications, not requests to generate images. The user wants advance warning when this conversation becomes very long so they can back up the current rules and resume in a new chat; exact context capacity cannot be measured, so warn when substantial context loss is becoming likely.
- Goldenrule.txt is the authoritative home for active quiz rules, quiz quality standards, workflows, and room-specific collaboration preferences. GitHub source files are authoritative for design and implemented behavior; backup/PMxmodule.txt is authoritative for subject, book, and chapter inventories. Keep these responsibilities separate. When a quiz or room-workflow rule changes, reconcile goldenrule.txt in the same task, replacing superseded rules instead of stacking conflicting versions.
- When proofreading existing quizzes, audit every currently playable subject and set, including question wording, answer options, answer keys, brief explanations, and any English translations. Check grammar, age-appropriateness, factual accuracy, single-answer ambiguity, Korean particles and sentence spacing, and alignment of translated question/options with the originals. Use natural US-style English and natural Korean or Malay as appropriate. Keep questions short and direct (for example, 'What does 사과 mean?' or 'Which sense organ helps us see?'); add response-method directions only when necessary. Never claim a full proof-check was completed if any playable bank or relevant field was skipped.

- Keep quiz questions short, simple and unambiguous. Add directions only when needed to explain how to respond (such as drag-and-drop, matching or ordering); avoid repetitive 'Choose the correct...' wording for obvious multiple-choice or fill-in questions. Korean questions must not include English sentence translations. For every subject, give brief, meaningful post-answer explanations rather than merely repeating the answer. Before publishing any Exercise, Quiz or Exam set, proofread every question, option, correct-answer key, explanation and available translation for natural, age-appropriate US English, Korean or Malay wording and factual consistency. Ensure translated options correspond exactly to the original options; preserve concise question wording and give a short reason for the answer.

sections.heading: EXAM CONTENT AND LEVEL RULES
sections.rules:
- When scanned textbooks/workbooks are supplied, derive subject-level quiz chapters from actual learning objectives and skills, not merely story, essay or theme titles printed as book units. Compare all relevant books, merge overlapping skills, and label chapters by what the student learns. Without scanned content (as with PM3 English and Malay), mark the chapter mapping unverified; never infer exact teaching scope from theme titles alone. Store resulting chapter names, mappings and source inventories only in the appropriate backup/PMxmodule.txt; this file records the method, not the chapter lists.
- Available school levels are PM3, PM4, PM5, PM6, SC1, SC2, SC3, SC4 and SC5. PM1 and PM2 are permanently excluded.
- Show a school-level option only when that subject/level has at least one real playable quiz. Show a chapter/revision option only when its question data and launch behavior exist. No empty buttons or unfinished placeholders.
- On entering a subject, initially show the available levels with 'Choose your level on top'. If none have content, show 'No quizzes available yet.' Selecting a level reveals only its available chapter/revision quizzes; reset the selection when entering a subject again.
- Existing Korean and Science PM3 Exam Revision question banks remain separate from future chapter-specific quizzes. Determine question counts from the actual data, not a hardcoded label.
- Future Science chapter content starts with Chapter 1 — Scientific Skills; other Science chapters and all Korean chapter names/content require the user's actual textbooks. Do not invent syllabus, objectives or textbook content, and do not pass revision questions off as chapter-specific questions.
- When textbooks are supplied, inspect their chapters and learning objectives, confirm unclear scope, and create accurate level/subject/chapter-specific question banks before exposing new chapter buttons.
- Write accurate age-appropriate questions with clear answers, meaningful distractors and explanations. Avoid unsupported syllabus claims, ambiguous choices and repetitive answer patterns. Default full revision volume is 30 questions unless the user specifies otherwise.
- Supported question types include multiple choice, selectable blanks, true/false, ordering, matching, drag/drop, text entry where requested and genuine picture-based questions. Korean and Science PM3 Exam Revision are currently no-typing, suitable for answering while travelling.
- Do not show unrelated emoji, decorative pictures or answer hints under questions. Genuine required question pictures must be relevant. All inputs, answers and drop zones must work within the question's available space, wrapping only when necessary. This is a functional responsiveness rule, not a visual specification.
- Choice taps submit answers immediately. Typed answers use Enter where enabled. Ordering submits once all items are placed; matching submits once all connections are made. Ordering supports drag/drop and tapping. Empty ordering zones may show instructions, but those instructions disappear once items are selected. Preserve Undo until submission.
- Correct/wrong feedback and explanations appear only after answer submission. Reviewing a previous answered question must not resubmit it or change its score.

sections.heading: BOOKMARK, NEXT AND RESUME BEHAVIOR
sections.rules:
- Next is normally disabled until the current question is answered. Bookmarking an unanswered question enables Next, allowing it to be skipped without scoring it wrong. Unanswered skipped questions remain available to complete later, and the quiz must not finish while unanswered questions remain.
- Bookmarks can be added/removed and opened from the bookmark list. The list auto-closes after approximately three seconds or an outside click; clicking inside it must not close it prematurely.
- Resume appears only when reviewing a previous bookmarked question. When clicked, Resume finds the first question that has not been answered (including previously bookmarked/skipped questions) and opens it. If every question has been answered, Resume automatically opens the score/results page. Preserve original answer and score snapshots during review.
- Exit returns to the quiz selection menu. Next advances according to answered/bookmarked state without skipping unreviewed work or prematurely ending the quiz.

sections.heading: EXAM TIMER AND RESULTS
sections.rules:
- Existing PM3 quiz timer uses three minutes per question. PM4+ Daily Quiz: 30 questions, 30 minutes per subject; Exam Revision: 30 questions, 90 minutes per subject. Apply timer by quiz type without changing existing PM3 quiz behavior. At five minutes remaining, show a dismissible time warning while countdown continues.
- Preserve score calculation, results screen, Try Again, Back Home and Download Score.
- Score report includes subject, quiz, score, date and incorrect question numbers/text. Avoid collecting unnecessary personal information.

sections.heading: BACKUP AND RECOVERY
sections.rules:
- Subject booklist, module, chapter and exam-scope inventories belong in separate year-specific files under backup/, e.g. backup/PM3module.txt and, when PM4 sources arrive, backup/PM4module.txt. Do not duplicate these inventories in goldenrule.txt. Keep each year file current: reconcile new source materials, replace superseded entries and remove retired data instead of accumulating contradictions.
- For a current source-and-assets backup, open https://github.com/dezinerj82/Quiz-room, select Code > Download ZIP and store it safely. This contains the tracked project files and visual design but not Git history.
- To preserve commit history too, use Git clone or a mirror clone and keep a separate secure copy. Never include access tokens/passwords.
- Before restoring a backup, compare it with current main and avoid overwriting newer work blindly.
- A future chat must fetch the latest goldenrule.txt and current GitHub files; do not rely on a stale saved prompt or screenshots.

sections.heading: QUIZ SOURCE MATERIALS AND EXAM PAPER TRANSCRIPTION
sections.rules:
- The user will supply exam scope (usually DOCX), scanned completed past exam papers (with pencil answers and teacher marks), scanned textbooks/workbooks, and scanned school booklists listing the books used per subject.
- Read source material carefully and cross-check scans against exam scope and books. For marked exam papers, reconstruct clean questions and answer choices without revealing pupil selections, teacher corrections, or marking. Do not copy handwritten marks into the quiz. Where scans are unclear, infer only when supported by context, flag uncertainty for review, and never silently invent an answer or claim certainty.
- PM3 source material is limited. PM4 onward should use the richer scope, booklist, textbooks, workbooks and completed past papers actually supplied. Proofread source questions, choices and correct answers; local textbooks may contain errors.

sections.heading: DAILY QUIZ — BIWEEKLY FROM 2027-01-03 (PM4 ONWARD)
sections.rules:
- Prepare and deploy once every two weeks on Sunday at 7:00 PM Malaysia time, anchored to Sunday 2027-01-03. The next preparation is 2027-01-17, then every 14 days. The quiz is intended for repeated practice during the following two weeks. This replaces the former Sunday–Thursday daily creation schedule.
- One new 30-question quiz per subject each two-week cycle; duration is 30 minutes per subject. First cycle: 30 questions on the opening chapter. Subsequent cycles: 25 fresh questions on the new chapter plus 5 fresh, nonduplicated review questions from the preceding cycle's chapter. Do not reuse exact question sentences or answer options merely to fill review slots.
- Plan the chapter sequence across roughly ten months (~22 two-week cycles), one new chapter per subject per cycle. The actual number of subjects and chapters depends on the supplied school booklist and learning content. Do not invent subjects or chapter counts; if there are more topics than cycles, consolidate related objectives carefully, without skipping essential content.
- For each subject, inspect the booklist and count modules/chapters/lesson units across its relevant textbooks and workbooks. Exclude books whose content requires physical handwriting, drawing or other hand-on-paper tasks that do not translate meaningfully to an onscreen quiz. Identify overlapping topics and group equivalent learning objectives across books into subject-level chapters with accurate, user-friendly labels, rather than copying each book's module divisions verbatim.
- Example: Get Smart Plus 3 Student Book has 10 modules, Workbook has 10 modules, and Grammar Makes Easy Year 3 has 17 major divisions spanning 95 lesson units. These are 37 major divisions before merging, not automatically 37 unique subject chapters; align actual overlapping content and fit appropriate chapters to the available cycles. Exclude Rampaian Praktis Mantap Cursive Writing Year 3 handwriting exercises.
- Stay close to verified textbook learning content and exam-style questions found in books. Adapt accurate book questions or write original questions, examples and short stories where needed for sufficient variety, provided the tested skill remains within the relevant learning objectives. Proofread and correct errors in locally produced books.
- Arrange a proof-check follow-up after each scheduled deployment, before the next practice period, to check question wording, choices, correct answers, explanations, chapter alignment and functionality. Never claim live deployment is confirmed without verification.

sections.heading: EXERCISE — ON-DEMAND WEAK-AREA PRACTICE
sections.rules:
- Exercise is a third quiz category alongside Daily Quiz and Exam Revision. It is created only when the user requests targeted practice for a particular weakness in a subject, and does not require the school booklist, textbook chapters or exam scope.
- Follow the user's specified weak area and ability level, including levels below the student's current school year (for example, kindergarten-level Malay vocabulary). Adapt difficulty and question formats to the actual need rather than assuming the school grade.
- Exercise sets must be organized under their actual subject (Math, English, Malay, Korean, Science, etc.), with separate topic/version choices within each subject. Never merge multiple subjects into a single Exercise subject or question bank.
- Each Exercise version contains exactly 10 questions. Create a descriptive topic label under the subject, with a sequential version number, e.g. English Exercise — Vocabulary 1, then English Exercise — Vocabulary 2.
- When another Exercise is requested for the same subject/topic, inspect all existing versions and generate 10 new, nonduplicated questions. Avoid repeating the same questions across versions, even if the learning objective is the same; vary wording, examples, answers and scenarios while staying on topic.
- Treat different weak areas as distinct Exercise topics with their own version numbering. Proofread answers and explanations before publishing.
- Only show an Exercise topic/version button when its actual playable question bank and launch behavior have been implemented. Do not add empty placeholder buttons. Preserve the existing website design and all Daily Quiz/Exam Revision behavior.
- No automatic Exercise generation schedule; user requests each version as needed.

sections.heading: EXAM REVISION — ONLY WHEN REQUESTED
sections.rules:
- Three school exams annually: Assessment, Middle Exam and Final Exam. Exam dates vary yearly; never schedule automatic exam revision generation.
- Assessment revision: use the teacher-provided exam scope and relevant textbook/workbook material (no prior assessment paper yet).
- Middle Exam revision: use the current exam scope, textbooks/workbooks and the completed Assessment paper.
- Final Exam revision: use the current exam scope, textbooks/workbooks and completed Assessment and Middle Exam papers.
- Each Exam Revision file contains exactly 30 questions per subject, with 1½ hours (90 minutes) per subject. Create one revision file/set per requested subject and exam only when the user asks, after the teacher distributes the exam scope (typically about a month before the exam). Map the exam scope to the booklist and relevant textbook/workbook learning content; verify sources before publishing.
- Exam Revision questions must not duplicate Daily Quiz questions verbatim. They may assess the same objective or use the same question format, but must use different sentences, examples, stories, values and answer choices as appropriate. Original questions are encouraged when educationally equivalent and within the exam scope.
- Keep Daily Quiz (30 minutes for 30 questions) and Exam Revision (90 minutes for 30 questions) timers separate. Preserve current PM3 behavior until a deliberate scoped implementation change.

sections.heading: CURRENT CONTENT
sections.rules: - Korean and Science PM3 Exam Revision quizzes exist. Other chapter/level options must be shown only after playable question content has actually been added.

sections.heading: PM3 TRANSITION EXCEPTION (UNTIL 2026-12-03)
sections.rules:
- PM3 ends on 2026-12-03. Until then, focus quiz content work on Korean, Malay and Math only.
- PM3 is an exceptional limited-source phase: the available booklist names books, but scanned textbook/workbook content is not available. Use only reliable available materials and established PM3 context; do not pretend to have read missing books or invent specific textbook chapters. Ask for source details when essential.
- The biweekly automated Daily Quiz creation and proof-check schedule starts with PM4 on 2027-01-03; do not apply that schedule to PM3. PM3 work is by request, not automatic daily generation.

- Post-answer English translations: For Malay, PJPK, and History (History begins PM4), show a smaller English translation directly below the question and smaller translations on the right of answer options only after the answer is submitted/revealed. Never translate the existing green-check/red-cross feedback symbols or their adjacent explanation text. Keep all other quiz behaviour unchanged. Each question needs verified English translation data; never show placeholder or invented translations.

sections.heading: SCORE REPORT — MANUAL GITHUB UPLOAD
sections.rules:
- Existing quiz gameplay and question banks remain unchanged. Score tracking starts fresh from 2026-10-29 with a new browser-local history namespace; no earlier results are imported.
- The home page has a monospace student-name input below Quiz Time. Press Enter to save the name on that browser. Each completed quiz automatically records exactly one attempt in browser localStorage, including subject, chapter/topic, completion time in Malaysia time, percentage, fraction, incorrect question numbers and unanswered numbers when applicable.
- Download Score produces a plain TXT file named username_subject_chapter_YYYYMMDD.txt with only lowercase ASCII letters, digits and underscores. Attempts for the same student/subject/chapter/date append in order; attempts on different dates create separate files. A second download includes all attempts recorded in that browser for the same file. Browser history is device/browser-specific and can be lost when site data is cleared; downloading is the durable backup.
- The user manually uploads TXT reports into the GitHub score/ folder. There is no automatic GitHub upload or external backend. Future analysis may compare missed question numbers and score trends. Once quiz content is published, preserve its question text/order for accurate tracking; introduce corrections or fresh questions as a new version instead.

sections.heading: ACTIVE GOLDEN RULE STORAGE POLICY
sections.rules:
- GitHub backup/Github rule.json records only active website functionality, processes, operational conditions and content rules. Never include personal data, user-specific accounts, credentials, private score data or ChatGPT memory instructions.
- Keep GitHub website rules in each repository's own backup/Github rule.json; do not treat one repository's file as the rule file for another repository.
- Personal context and ChatGPT-specific workflows belong in the relevant ChatGPT Project source, not in public GitHub files. Updates to Project sources require an available supported write mechanism; do not claim unattended or periodic updates without a configured automation and verified destination.
- Reconcile rules when requirements change: remove retired, invalid, cancelled and superseded rules. Preserve only currently active, valid requirements.
